shape: Fresh session, first and only cycle. Driver-only: no subagent was warranted because the work was one tight measure-edit-rebuild loop on a single manuscript, where every candidate edit had to be scored against three gates that only a rebuild can evaluate. Handing that to a seat would have paid a worktree round trip per variant and returned a verdict the driver would have had to re-measure anyway.
took: AUT-PD-106 (claimed via claim.py, CLAIMED on attempt 1) -- the two red manuscript-tier gates on the ASO journal article. Independently confirmed as this cycle's correct work before taking it: the completed CI run preceding main's head was conclusion=failure, and both gates were reproduced on a clean origin/main with this session's work stashed. research-loop §1 makes a red trunk the cycle.
took_what: Both gates are green on the tree committed: journal PDF 7 -> 6 typeset pages, and justification 13/383 blown lines (33.94 per 1,000) -> 8/376 (21.28) against a 23.5 ceiling. Neither ceiling was touched. The route to it was measurement, not reasoning: a bisect established the page budget needed ~8 more words than the apparatus cut freed and that words removed late in the flow are worth more than words removed on page 4; a five-way variant harness scored each candidate rewording against all three gates, and three of the five candidates made justification WORSE by lowering the median (the threshold is 2x the median, so a tighter build counts more lines as blown). One candidate that passed on metrics was rejected on meaning.

what_i_got_wrong: THE ROW'S NAMED DESTINATION, AND I NEARLY FOLLOWED IT. AUT-PD-106 said to relocate the apparatus 'to the SI'. The journal article has no SI -- build_submission_pdf.py says so in terms -- and the file by that name belongs to the extended report. Moving a result there would have deleted it from the submission while looking like a relocation. Caught by reading the builder's PAPERS entry before editing, not by the gates, which would all have stayed green.
